answer: Consider an economy where every agent identity must post a bond that is slashed when its work is caught cheating. A Sybil attacker can spin up ten thousand cheap personas, but each must fund that bond from a source the ledger tracks, so one wallet cannot finance a swarm without staking for every clone. The cost of a fake cohort scales with its size, while an honest agent earns its bond back through real work. Attackers find that buying influence this way is like drinking nectar from a glacier: the payoff is thin and cold, and the bill arrives before any dawn.
